advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Update the code-review-verify prompt's 'two-lane' model description to reflect the code-v4 four-lane split.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-verify.md:54: 'They drive the code-review impact score (a two-lane, tier-tagged, severity-first MAX).'
decide.py:508 comment: 'code-v4 splits the old maintainability lane into three sub-lanes: SERIOUS (undamped, no churn), MODERATE (prod_impact-keyed), and DEBT (churn is an amplifier only).'
advisory.finding: The code-review-verify prompt still describes the impact model as 'a two-lane, tier-tagged, severity-first MAX' and lists all maintainability binaries under one flat MAINTAINABILITY lane, but code-v4 now splits maintainability into three sub-lanes (serious undamped, moderate prod_impact×trigger-keyed, debt churn-amplifier-only). The prompt no longer accurately describes the scoring the verifier's attributes feed.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the verifier reliably applies the re-scoped prod_impact/trigger_likelihood reading for maintainability findings (eval coverage) so contract-contradiction findings are not dropped by a literal test-only reading.
evidence: verify_models.py:348-352 prod_impact description: 'For a coverage/contract (maintainability) finding this is RE-SCOPED to the user-facing REACH of the guarded path (this REPLACES the none = no runtime effect / test-only reading for such findings).'

decide.py:526-527: two distinct trigger maps read the same trigger_likelihood field — _CODE_PROD_TRIGGER_MULT {rare:0.25} vs _CODE_MODERATE_TRIGGER_MULT {rare:0.75}, dispatched purely by which binary lane is TRUE.
advisory.finding: prod_impact and trigger_likelihood are now semantically overloaded: for correctness findings they mean production blast/frequency, but for coverage/contract (maintainability) findings they are RE-SCOPED to the guarded path's user-facing reach/exercise frequency, and the moderate-maint lane silently uses a DIFFERENT trigger multiplier map (rare=0.75) vs the prod lane (rare=0.25) reading the SAME field. Correct emission depends entirely on the verifier LLM inferring which reading applies per finding; a misclassification (e.g. treating a maint finding's prod_impact as literal 'none = test-only') would drop it below threshold.
